items.title: David Robinson says a sense of 'cognitive dissonance' led him to leave OpenAI
items.summary: David Robinson said he experienced 'cognitive dissonance' at OpenAI, which led him to leave the company. World Economic Forum David Robinson said that despite advocating for slowdowns, OpenAI was racing ahead with development. The disconnect produced in Robinson a sense of "cognitive dissonance," he said. Robinson quit the company last week, saying that the AI giant isn't being careful enough. David Robinson says OpenAI was saying one thing while doing another. Robinson, formerly a leader on OpenAI's Safety Systems team, sat down with Ezra Klein for The New York Times' "The Ezra Klein Show" for his first interview since quitting the AI company last week. Robinson told Klein that, despite repeated warnings about the capabilities of new models and expressing interest in slowing down AI development , OpenAI was moving as fast as ever behind the scenes. "Part of what was the fundamental cognitive dissonance for me was we keep publishing these warnings, but ultimately, we're still training and deploying these dangerous models that we're warning about," Robinson said. In July, hundreds of OpenAI employees signed an open letter titled " Pacing the Frontier ," which urged the government to impose regulations that would slow down AI development. Then, in September, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said he agreed with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, who had earlier published an essay advocating that AI companies coordinate a slowdown among themselves. "We need to pace the frontier," Altman said at the time on X. "This has been a primary topic of discussions we've had at OpenAI in recent weeks." Within OpenAI's office, though, Robinson told Klein that there was continued "frenetic" activity and that people were "running on fumes." "It feels almost like a ballet or a kind of dance because all these different functions are kind of all streaming together," he said of OpenAI. "There's a lot of adrenaline." Researchers at OpenAI have been rather frank about the dangers of letting AI build itself, a process called recursive self-improvement, or RSI. "This is a time that calls for extreme caution," Jakub Pachocki, OpenAI's chief scientist, said in a blog post about RSI in September. OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment for this article. An OpenAI spokesperson previously said, in response to an essay Robinson wrote in The Atlantic, that the company is taking steps to improve security for its AI models. "As our models become more capable, we continue to strengthen our safety and security practices to address the risks we see today while building safety cases to anticipate the risks of future advances," the spokesperson said. "We're making sure our models don't become more capable than we can safely manage and secure, and we pause training or hold back models when we need to slow down." items.title: Forecasting Demand for New Products
items.summary: Source: Photo by Kathy Jones from Pexels Solving cold-start forecasting with classic ML: from baseline to transfer learning for gradient boosting TL;DR Forecasting demand is a popular, but often challenging task in retail, e-commerce and logistics domains. The article describes undertaken approaches for forecasting new products: from baseline to a more complex modelling. The best accuracy was achieved using Transfer Learning: the model trained on regular products was further trained on new products. $WAPE was improved from 70% on baseline to 36%. While many articles, examples, and tutorials show how to forecast demand for regular products, few resources cover new products. This article documents a real-world case of forecasting approaches for new products. Forecasting demand Forecasting demand is an important task for any business. An accurate forecast allows business to develop its financial plan, optimize logistics deliveries, and prepare marketing campaigns. It helps reduce operational costs and support product availability, which leads to customer retention and ultimately customer lifetime value (CLTV) growth. New or temporary products can increase additional sales, which contributes to a significant share of total revenue. Every successful launch requires assessing demand. Therefore, forecasting sales of new products is an important task for retail and logistics businesses. Characteristics of new products The main difference between new products and regular ones is that they do not have lag features such as `last_week_sales`. This feature is, firstly, a good forecast in itself (if the time series has weekly seasonality), and secondly, one of the most important features for any forecasting model. Without it, accuracy drops significantly. In this article, new products are products that have no sales history for creating lag features. These include products that 1) have never existed or been sold before and 2) seasonal products that stop selling after the season ends. New products can be 1) completely new or 2) similar to existing products that have just one new feature substituted or added (new syrup in coffee). Sales volume of new products 1) may be negligible or 2) may exceed the volume of regular products (Figure 1). New product launches are often paired with marketing promotions. These promotions push new product sales above those of regular products. However, sometimes new products are launched simply to expand the product range. Such products aren’t necessarily popular, and their sales are, conversely, lower than those of regular products. Figure 1. An example of a product launch that outsold its regular alternative. Therefore, forecasting new products in the same way as regular products is impossible and requires separate forecasting models. Without lag features, a model has no direct signal of how much a product is likely to sell. This gap must be filled by other means: Product similarity provides the most important information: a new product sharing key attributes with an established one is likely to exhibit a comparable sales pattern. Marketing features and popularity markers capture factors that drive demand independently of past sales. Together, these signals suggest that forecasting new products is best approached not through time-series extrapolation, but through comparison with structurally similar, already-observed products. Forecasting approaches This section presents the approaches used to forecast new product demand. For each approach, approximate $WAPE scores are attached to evaluate influence on business. This metric weights each sample by its true cost, so expensive elements contribute more to the final score than cheap ones. That characteristic makes $WAPE better aligned with retail and e-commerce businesses’ unit economics. Figure 2. WAPE metric formula Baseline The initial approach is to assign a coefficient of popularity for each new product: how many “units per customer” (UPC) would be sold each day. UPC coefficient is fairly stable and can be estimated manually by calculating the UPC of similar products. Sales forecasts could be obtained by multiplying UPC by the “number of customers” (NOC): sales = NOC * UPC . NOC is usually a well-predicted value by standard autoregressive models, like SARIMA or Prophet. In this approach, UPC covers the magnitude of sales, while NOC covers intraweek seasonality. Result: The accuracy of the resulting forecast was quite poor ($WAPE > 70%). But this approach has several drawbacks: The UPC value can still vary slightly across time and region; There is no straightforward algorithm for calculating UPC for new products; The sales forecast is obtained by multiplying two forecast values, which increases the calculation error; In practice, the accuracy of the resulting forecast is poor. UPC calculation improvement We can keep the same modelling approach, but improve UPC calculation. We want to predict UPC with ML. Moreover, since UPC changes over time, we want to predict it weekly. The data for both regular products and previously launched new products is used to easily calculate weekly UPC. Features are product categories and specifications, time-derived features, and a flag indicating whether the product is new or not. The evaluation is made by retraining the ML model before each product release and estimating forecasts for the first week after the launch. Here, a Gradient Boosting model can be used. For cases of many categorical values, CatBoost is recommended. Result: Final sales forecasts with predicted UPCs had $WAPE 45-55%. Training time and computing resources were low. This approach still has several drawbacks: Even during the first week, the sales can grow significantly day-to-day, and that is not represented by UPC. The sales forecast is still obtained by multiplying two predicted values, which increases the calculation error; The forecasting accuracy is still quite poor. What if we tried to predict the final sales figures with one model without intermediate values calculation (UPC)? One-model approach The data of regular sales and the history of new product launches over the past year were used. Similar features describing product categories and specifications, time-derived features, and a “new product” flag were used. No lag features were calculated. Result: model showed similar metric as improved baseline approach ($WAPE 50%). The dataset size grew significantly, increasing training time and computing resources. The main drawback of this approach is class imbalance in the data. There are significantly more regular sales than new product launches (100:1). Two standard solutions (downsampling and upsampling) were tested. Result: Downsampling led to a decrease in model accuracy. Upsampling and combination of approaches also did not improve accuracy ($WAPE 50%). Upsampling required significantly more RAM. Synthetic data generation was not considered a reasonable approach here. However, the problem could be solved with knowledge transfer learning: training on the large dataset of regular products, and then fine-tuning on just new launches. Transfer learning approach The Transfer Learning method for gradient boosting models is fairly simple to implement. The data was divided into two partitions (regular products and new products). The data features have to be identical for both parts. Thus, the first model (model) is trained on regular sales to account for seasonality, regional specificity, and the distribution of sales between product groups. The second model (fine_tuned_model) corrects the errors of the first model to forecast new products based on the changed sales distribution. The first model was trained on regular products with a high learning_rate of 0.025 and a small number of trees (n_estimators = 100). The second model was trained on new products with a low learning_rate of 0.01 and a large number of trees (n_estimators = 750). Result: Final sales forecasts with the model after first-step training: $WAPE 52%. After second-step training: $WAPE 36%. Training time and computing resources were comparable with the previous approaches. CatBoost with transfer learning Here is the implementation of the transfer learning approach for training CatBoost regression model: # 1st model: trained on regular products model = cb.CatBoostRegressor(**params_1) model.fit( X_train_1, y_train_1, eval_set=(X_eval_1, y_eval_1), early_stopping_rounds=50, ) # 2nd model: fine-tuned on new products fine_tuned_model = cb.CatBoostRegressor(**params_2) fine_tuned_model.fit( X_train_2, y_train_2, eval_set=(X_eval_2, y_eval_2), early_stopping_rounds=50, init_model=model, ) Conclusions Forecasting new products is a hard problem. Without a sales history, most standard time-series features — including lag features — are unavailable. There is no single best solution, but several approaches offer useful trade-offs. Here is a recap of the approaches that were tested: Baseline two-step modelling. We started with a simple baseline: sales = number of customers (NOC) × units per customer (UPC). NOC was predicted with a standard autoregressive model; UPC was estimated manually. This baseline produced forecasts quickly, but its accuracy was poor (WAPE above 70%). UPC estimation with ML model significantly improved the quality of predictions ($WAPE 45–55%). Basis single-step modelling. Two-step approaches, like the baseline, combine two separate forecasts into one. Each forecast carries its own error, and multiplying them together compounds these errors. Predicting sales directly, in a single step, avoids this problem. However, class imbalance limits the model’s ability to capture patterns associated with new products ($WAPE 50%). Single-step modelling: CatBoost with transfer learning . Transfer learning goes further: instead of predicting sales from scratch, it predicts the residual — the correction needed on top of an existing forecast. This preserves the accuracy of the base model while still adapting to new products. This approach improved $WAPE from 52% to 36% — the best result of all approaches tested, at no added computational cost. Forecasting Demand for New Products was originally published in Towards AI on Medium, where people are continuing the conversation by highlighting and responding to this story.
items.summary_html:
Source: Photo by Kathy Jones from PexelsSolving cold-start forecasting with classic ML: from baseline to transfer learning for gradient boostingTL;DR
Forecasting demand is a popular, but often challenging task in retail, e-commerce and logistics domains. The article describes undertaken approaches for forecasting new products: from baseline to a more complex modelling. The best accuracy was achieved using Transfer Learning: the model trained on regular products was further trained on new products. $WAPE was improved from 70% on baseline to 36%.

While many articles, examples, and tutorials show how to forecast demand for regular products, few resources cover new products. This article documents a real-world case of forecasting approaches for new products.

Forecasting demand

Forecasting demand is an important task for any business. An accurate forecast allows business to develop its financial plan, optimize logistics deliveries, and prepare marketing campaigns. It helps reduce operational costs and support product availability, which leads to customer retention and ultimately customer lifetime value (CLTV) growth.

New or temporary products can increase additional sales, which contributes to a significant share of total revenue. Every successful launch requires assessing demand. Therefore, forecasting sales of new products is an important task for retail and logistics businesses.

Characteristics of new products

The main difference between new products and regular ones is that they do not have lag features such as `last_week_sales`. This feature is, firstly, a good forecast in itself (if the time series has weekly seasonality), and secondly, one of the most important features for any forecasting model. Without it, accuracy drops significantly.

In this article, new products are products that have no sales history for creating lag features. These include products that 1) have never existed or been sold before and 2) seasonal products that stop selling after the season ends.

New products can be 1) completely new or 2) similar to existing products that have just one new feature substituted or added (new syrup in coffee).

Sales volume of new products 1) may be negligible or 2) may exceed the volume of regular products (Figure 1). New product launches are often paired with marketing promotions. These promotions push new product sales above those of regular products. However, sometimes new products are launched simply to expand the product range. Such products aren’t necessarily popular, and their sales are, conversely, lower than those of regular products.

Figure 1. An example of a product launch that outsold its regular alternative.

Therefore, forecasting new products in the same way as regular products is impossible and requires separate forecasting models. Without lag features, a model has no direct signal of how much a product is likely to sell. This gap must be filled by other means:

  • Product similarity provides the most important information: a new product sharing key attributes with an established one is likely to exhibit a comparable sales pattern.
  • Marketing features and popularity markers capture factors that drive demand independently of past sales.

Together, these signals suggest that forecasting new products is best approached not through time-series extrapolation, but through comparison with structurally similar, already-observed products.

Forecasting approaches
This section presents the approaches used to forecast new product demand. For each approach, approximate $WAPE scores are attached to evaluate influence on business.
This metric weights each sample by its true cost, so expensive elements contribute more to the final score than cheap ones. That characteristic makes $WAPE better aligned with retail and e-commerce businesses’ unit economics.
Figure 2. WAPE metric formulaBaseline

The initial approach is to assign a coefficient of popularity for each new product: how many “units per customer” (UPC) would be sold each day. UPC coefficient is fairly stable and can be estimated manually by calculating the UPC of similar products.

Sales forecasts could be obtained by multiplying UPC by the “number of customers” (NOC): sales = NOC * UPC. NOC is usually a well-predicted value by standard autoregressive models, like SARIMA or Prophet. In this approach, UPC covers the magnitude of sales, while NOC covers intraweek seasonality.

Result: The accuracy of the resulting forecast was quite poor ($WAPE > 70%).

But this approach has several drawbacks:

  • The UPC value can still vary slightly across time and region;
  • There is no straightforward algorithm for calculating UPC for new products;
  • The sales forecast is obtained by multiplying two forecast values, which increases the calculation error;
  • In practice, the accuracy of the resulting forecast is poor.
UPC calculation improvement

We can keep the same modelling approach, but improve UPC calculation. We want to predict UPC with ML. Moreover, since UPC changes over time, we want to predict it weekly.

The data for both regular products and previously launched new products is used to easily calculate weekly UPC. Features are product categories and specifications, time-derived features, and a flag indicating whether the product is new or not.

The evaluation is made by retraining the ML model before each product release and estimating forecasts for the first week after the launch. Here, a Gradient Boosting model can be used. For cases of many categorical values, CatBoost is recommended.

Result: Final sales forecasts with predicted UPCs had $WAPE 45-55%. Training time and computing resources were low.

This approach still has several drawbacks:

  • Even during the first week, the sales can grow significantly day-to-day, and that is not represented by UPC.
  • The sales forecast is still obtained by multiplying two predicted values, which increases the calculation error;
  • The forecasting accuracy is still quite poor.

What if we tried to predict the final sales figures with one model without intermediate values calculation (UPC)?

One-model approach

The data of regular sales and the history of new product launches over the past year were used. Similar features describing product categories and specifications, time-derived features, and a “new product” flag were used. No lag features were calculated.

Result: model showed similar metric as improved baseline approach ($WAPE 50%). The dataset size grew significantly, increasing training time and computing resources.

The main drawback of this approach is class imbalance in the data. There are significantly more regular sales than new product launches (100:1). Two standard solutions (downsampling and upsampling) were tested.

Result: Downsampling led to a decrease in model accuracy. Upsampling and combination of approaches also did not improve accuracy ($WAPE 50%). Upsampling required significantly more RAM.

Synthetic data generation was not considered a reasonable approach here. However, the problem could be solved with knowledge transfer learning: training on the large dataset of regular products, and then fine-tuning on just new launches.

Transfer learning approach

The Transfer Learning method for gradient boosting models is fairly simple to implement. The data was divided into two partitions (regular products and new products). The data features have to be identical for both parts.

Thus, the first model (model) is trained on regular sales to account for seasonality, regional specificity, and the distribution of sales between product groups. The second model (fine_tuned_model) corrects the errors of the first model to forecast new products based on the changed sales distribution.

The first model was trained on regular products with a high learning_rate of 0.025 and a small number of trees (n_estimators = 100). The second model was trained on new products with a low learning_rate of 0.01 and a large number of trees (n_estimators = 750).

Result: Final sales forecasts with the model after first-step training: $WAPE 52%. After second-step training: $WAPE 36%. Training time and computing resources were comparable with the previous approaches.
CatBoost with transfer learning

Here is the implementation of the transfer learning approach for training CatBoost regression model:

# 1st model: trained on regular products
model = cb.CatBoostRegressor(**params_1)
model.fit(
    X_train_1, 
    y_train_1,
    eval_set=(X_eval_1, y_eval_1),
    early_stopping_rounds=50,
)

# 2nd model: fine-tuned on new products
fine_tuned_model = cb.CatBoostRegressor(**params_2)
fine_tuned_model.fit(
    X_train_2, 
    y_train_2,
    eval_set=(X_eval_2, y_eval_2),
    early_stopping_rounds=50,
    init_model=model,
)
Conclusions

Forecasting new products is a hard problem. Without a sales history, most standard time-series features — including lag features — are unavailable. There is no single best solution, but several approaches offer useful trade-offs. Here is a recap of the approaches that were tested:

  • Baseline two-step modelling. We started with a simple baseline: sales = number of customers (NOC) × units per customer (UPC). NOC was predicted with a standard autoregressive model; UPC was estimated manually. This baseline produced forecasts quickly, but its accuracy was poor (WAPE above 70%). UPC estimation with ML model significantly improved the quality of predictions ($WAPE 45–55%).
  • Basis single-step modelling. Two-step approaches, like the baseline, combine two separate forecasts into one. Each forecast carries its own error, and multiplying them together compounds these errors. Predicting sales directly, in a single step, avoids this problem. However, class imbalance limits the model’s ability to capture patterns associated with new products ($WAPE 50%).
  • Single-step modelling: CatBoost with transfer learning. Transfer learning goes further: instead of predicting sales from scratch, it predicts the residual — the correction needed on top of an existing forecast. This preserves the accuracy of the base model while still adapting to new products. This approach improved $WAPE from 52% to 36% — the best result of all approaches tested, at no added computational cost.

Forecasting Demand for New Products was originally published in Towards AI on Medium, where people are continuing the conversation by highlighting and responding to this story.

items.title: Finland Orders Google to Suspend New Data Centers After Contractors Pave Over Protected Forests
items.summary: Finish environmental authorities are in a rage over Google’s $15 billion data center projects after the discovery that company contractors had chopped down some 330 hectares of government-protected forests, seemingly without a permit. According to Agence France-Presse , the Finnish Supervisory Agency (LVV) demanded that the Google-affiliate company Tuike Finland Oy “immediately suspend… all preparatory measures that would significantly alter the environment” in connection with two planned data center developments in the Northern municipalities of Muhos and Kajaani. In all, LVV accuses Google’s contractor of clear-cutting some 330 hectares in Muhos without completing a mandatory environmental impact assessment, a necessary step for receiving approval. The company cleared a further 200 hectares for its data center in Kajaani, though it isn’t clear whether that logging was approved by authorities. As the Guardian reported , Google has just over a week to explain its actions to Finnish officials. Though a government review is only just getting underway, the tech giant is already expressing remorse. In a statement to AFP , Google spokesperson Sondre Ronander admitted the company messed up, saying “we understand the concerns and have fallen short of our own high standards in this instance.” “We will study the LVV’s findings and follow their guidance,” Ronander continued. As head of the environmental department of the LVV Tommi Muilu told AFP , Google has not only felled hundreds of acres of trees, but has stripped topsoil, engineered roads and storage areas, and altered ditches. Speaking to AFP , chair of the long-running Finnish Association for Nature Conservation said Google had paved over “nature sites which should be preserved.” More on data centers: Amazon Warns Local Communities to Stop Defying Its Massive AI Data Centers

items.title: Kubernetes won the orchestration wars. Its teams are still fighting.
items.summary: Kubernetes won the container orchestration wars. The CNCF reports that 82% of container users run Kubernetes in production. Despite its market dominance, Kubernetes teams aren’t always happy. It turns out that keeping developers and operations teams happy takes more than agreeing on which technology to use. Developers appreciate Kubernetes self-service capabilities, which allow them to scale apps and tweak configurations without external approval. Operations teams often sweat the very same capabilities, or as our guest, HPE Fellow David Estes puts it, “operations teams have always wanted to slow things down,” as they favor stability, ticketing, and change requests. Developers, in contrast, “want to move fast.” At the same time, apps are spreading across hybrid and edge computing environments as AI inference workloads soar, further stressing Kubernetes-using teams. Estes also thinks many companies lean too heavily on microservices, leading to “architecture bloat.” So, what’s the fix? The good news is that while AI workloads are forcing companies to handle GPU scheduling and capacity scaling to handle demand spikes, AI automation may resolve some of the issues the technology is causing. Estes reckons that developers will be able to use AI automation to monitor Kubernetes clusters, check logs, and perhaps “predict if there’s going to be an outage.” Operationally, using AI to automate some infra tasks could be “huge” for the Kubernetes landscape, the Fellow said. HPE has created software to help resolve the Kubernetes issues we discuss – HPE OpsRamp to help manage multi-cloud and on-prem computing environments, for example – but beyond particular products, it’s encouraging to hear that AI itself may be able to remedy some of the new challenges its uptake has created. That means that no matter what software the modern developer and their operations counterpart use, they should be able to untangle their containerization snarls. Given how popular — and I would add economy-critical — Kubernetes is today, that’s good news for us all. HPE is heading to KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America in Salt Lake City (Nov. 9–12) and other events, and would love to say hi.

items.title: Every public appearance Melania Trump has made during Donald Trump's second White House term — and what she wore
items.summary: First lady Melania Trump broke with tradition by wearing pants to a state dinner held in honor of Chinese leader Xi Jinping. Yuri Gripas/CNP/Bloomberg via Getty Images Melania Trump is an enigmatic first lady who has, at times, been an infrequent White House presence. There was a 32-day stretch this summer where she did not make any public appearances. Recently, she spoke at an event at the Rose Garden and joined the president at a state dinner. Melania Trump has been known as an enigmatic first lady since President Donald Trump's first term, but her public appearances and outfit choices can provide a window into her approach to the role. Ahead of the 2025 inauguration, Melania Trump told Fox News that she planned to divide her time between the White House, Trump Tower in New York City, and Mar-a-Lago in Palm Beach, Florida. This schedule has at times made her an infrequent presence at the White House. Over the summer, there was a 32-day stretch from mid-July to mid-August where she did not make any public appearances. However, she has attended numerous events during Donald Trump's second, non-consecutive term, such as the premiere of her "Melania" documentary, King Charles and Queen Camilla's state visit, and appearances promoting her Fostering the Future and Presidential AI Challenge initiatives. Melania Trump's muted fashion choices could also indicate a more guarded approach to the role of first lady. At White House events, she has largely appeared wearing suits and neutral basics in black, beige, cream, and gray. It's a departure from the bold outfits she often chose during Donald Trump's first term. A spokesperson for the Office of the first lady declined to comment. First lady Melania Trump broke with tradition by wearing pants to a state dinner held in honor of Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

Yuri Gripas/CNP/Bloomberg via Getty Images

  • Melania Trump is an enigmatic first lady who has, at times, been an infrequent White House presence.
  • There was a 32-day stretch this summer where she did not make any public appearances.
  • Recently, she spoke at an event at the Rose Garden and joined the president at a state dinner.

Melania Trump has been known as an enigmatic first lady since President Donald Trump's first term, but her public appearances and outfit choices can provide a window into her approach to the role.

Ahead of the 2025 inauguration, Melania Trump told Fox News that she planned to divide her time between the White House, Trump Tower in New York City, and Mar-a-Lago in Palm Beach, Florida.

This schedule has at times made her an infrequent presence at the White House. Over the summer, there was a 32-day stretch from mid-July to mid-August where she did not make any public appearances.

However, she has attended numerous events during Donald Trump's second, non-consecutive term, such as the premiere of her "Melania" documentary, King Charles and Queen Camilla's state visit, and appearances promoting her Fostering the Future and Presidential AI Challenge initiatives.

Melania Trump's muted fashion choices could also indicate a more guarded approach to the role of first lady. At White House events, she has largely appeared wearing suits and neutral basics in black, beige, cream, and gray. It's a departure from the bold outfits she often chose during Donald Trump's first term.

A spokesperson for the Office of the first lady declined to comment.

Take a look at the first lady's White House activities and appearances thus far.

January 20, 2025: Melania Trump attended the inauguration.
US President Donald Trump (L) and First Lady Melania Trump arrive for the Liberty inaugural ball in Washington, DC, on January 20, 2025.

JIM WATSON/AFP via Getty Images

Melania Trump held the Bible as Donald Trump was sworn in for his second non-consecutive term, and the couple danced together at several inaugural balls later that evening.

For the swearing-in ceremony, Melania Trump wore a navy coat and skirt by Adam Lippes, an American designer. She accessorized with a matching wide-brimmed hat by Eric Javits.

Her black-and-white inaugural gown was designed by Hervé Pierre.

January 21, 2025: The president and first lady joined Vice President JD Vance and Usha Vance at the National Prayer Service.
U.S. President Donald Trump, first lady Melania and U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance with second lady Usha attend the National Day of Prayer Service at the Washington National Cathedral in Washington, U.S., January 21, 2025.

Kevin Lamarque/REUTERS

The service, the last of Donald Trump's inaugural events, was held at the Washington National Cathedral in Washington, DC.

January 24, 2025: Melania Trump and Donald Trump visited California and North Carolina to survey damage caused by natural disasters.
U.S. President Donald Trump and first lady Melania Trump attend a briefing on wildfire damage as they visit the Pacific Palisades neighborhood that was damaged by the Palisades Fire, in Los Angeles, California, U.S., January 24, 2025.

Leah Millis/REUTERS

Melania Trump joined Donald Trump to visit Los Angeles in the aftermath of multiple wildfires and neighborhoods in North Carolina damaged by Hurricane Helene.

Together, they met with first responders and residents who had lost their homes and businesses. Melania Trump was photographed hugging and shaking hands with those affected by the natural disasters.

February 22, 2025: Donald Trump and Melania Trump hosted the National Governors Association dinner at the White House.
US President Donald Trump and US First Lady Melania Trump arrive for the National Governors Association Evening Dinner and Reception in the East Room of the White House in Washington, DC, on February 22, 2025.

ROBERTO SCHMIDT/AFP via Getty Images

Melania Trump wore a black Dolce & Gabbana tuxedo, similar to the outfit she chose for her official White House portrait, while posing for photos with governors from across the US.

Donald Trump thanked Melania Trump in his speech, saying that she "made the evening beautiful."

March 3, 2025: She participated in a roundtable discussion on the "TAKE IT DOWN" Act targeting revenge porn.
U.S. first lady Melania Trump, U.S. Senator Ted Cruz (R-TX) and Elliston Berry attend a roundtable discussion on the "Take it Down Act," a legislation against revenge porn, on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C., U.S., March 3, 2025.

Kent Nishimura/REUTERS

"TAKE IT DOWN" is an acronym for "Tools to Address Known Exploitation by Immobilizing Technological Deepfakes on Websites and Networks."

The act criminalizes the publication of non-consensual intimate imagery, including AI-generated deepfakes, and requires websites to remove them.

"Every young person deserves a safe online space to express themself freely, without the looming threat of exploitation or harm," Melania Trump said in her opening remarks.

She wore a tan three-piece suit by Ralph Lauren with a black tie.

March 4, 2025: Melania Trump attended Donald Trump's speech to a joint session of Congress.
First Lady of the U.S. Melania Trump waves on the day of U.S. President Donald Trump's speech to a joint session of Congress, in the House Chamber of the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C., U.S., March 4, 2025.

Kevin Lamarque/REUTERS

The first lady's guests included the families of Corey Comperatore, the firefighter who was fatally shot during an assassination attempt against Donald Trump in Butler, Pennsylvania, and Laken Riley, who was killed by a man who had entered the US illegally.

Melania Trump wore a gray skirt suit by Dior.

Melania Trump, joined by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, presented awards to several notable women in a ceremony held at the State Department. She wore a leopard-print coat designed by Milly Park.

"These extraordinary women illuminate the transformative power of love in shaping our world," she said in her remarks at the event. "Their journeys remind us that true courage is born from a deep commitment to others, showing that love fuels the call for justice."

WASHINGTON, DC - MAY 19: U.S. President Donald Trump and first lady Melania Trump arrive at the signing ceremony for the TAKE IT DOWN Act in the Rose Garden of the White House on May 19, 2025 in Washington, DC. The first lady made the Tools to Address Known Exploitation by Immobilizing Technological Deepfakes on Websites and Networks (TAKE IT DOWN) Act a priority, traveling to Capitol Hill to lobby lawmakers and show her support for the legislation, which addresses non-consensual intimate imagery, or "revenge porn," and artificial intelligence deepfakes posted online and to social media.

Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images

The bill, which was first presented to Congress in 2024 before Donald Trump took office, received widespread bipartisan support.

"Artificial intelligence and social media are the digital candy for the next generation: sweet, addictive, and engineered to have an impact on the cognitive development of our children," Melania Trump said in her remarks at the signing ceremony.

The first lady wore a gray Prada suit for the event.

May 20, 2025: Melania Trump hosted a Take Our Daughters and Sons to Work Day event for children in the Kennedy Garden.
U.S. first lady Melania Trump hosts a Take Our Daughters and Sons to Work Day event at the White House in Washington, D.C., U.S., May 20, 2025.

The first lady greeted the children of White House staffers as they participated in an arts-and-crafts activity.

"It is always special to see children's creativity and spirit on display, especially here at the White House where so many hardworking men and women support the success of our nation every day," she said in a White House statement.

May 21, 2025: She spoke at the Senate Spouses Luncheon held at the National Gallery of Art.
Melania Trump at the Senate Spouses Luncheon at the National Gallery of Art.

June 14, 2025: Melania Trump attended the US Army's 250th anniversary parade alongside Donald Trump.

US First Lady Melania Trump on April 9 made a surprise on-camera statement to deny unspecified allegations about her and convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. "The lies linking me with the disgraceful Jeffrey Epstein need to end today," she said. "The individuals lying about me are devoid of ethical standards, humility and respect."

Mandel NGAN/AFP via Getty Images

Melania Trump said that Epstein did not introduce her to Donald Trump, that she "never had a relationship" with Epstein or Ghislaine Maxwell, and that she was "not Epstein's victim" and had no knowledge of his abuse.

"The lies linking me with the disgraceful Jeffrey Epstein need to end today," she said.

April 13, 2026: Donald Trump and Melania Trump greeted King Willem-Alexander and Queen Màxima of the Netherlands at the White House.
WASHINGTON, DC - APRIL 13: U.S. President Donald Trump (Center, R) and first lady Melania Trump (R) greet King Willem-Alexander and Queen Màxima of the Netherlands at the Diplomatic Entrance of the White House on April 13, 2026 in Washington, DC. The Dutch king and queen are set to stay overnight at the White House as part of a three-day trip to the U.S. with stops in Philadelphia and Miami.

Win McNamee/Getty Images

Melania Trump wore a black-and-white Erdem gown to greet the Dutch royals, who visited the White House as part of a three-day trip to the US.

April 15, 2026: Melania Trump spoke at a roundtable discussion about the foster care system with the House Ways and Means Committee.
WASHINGTON, DC - APRIL 15: First Lady Melania Trump listens as Chairman Jason Smith (R-MO) gives opening remarks at a roundtable discussion with the House Ways and Means Committee on the foster care system, at the Longworth House Office Building in Washington, DC on April 15, 2026.

Nathan Posner/Anadolu via Getty Images

Melania Trump advocated for legislation related to "housing instability, educational advocacy, financial barriers, transportation, continuity, access to technology, and other related issues" in the foster care system.

She wore a beige pantsuit.

April 23, 2026: She was joined by Usha Vance at the annual First Lady's Luncheon.
Second Lady Usha Vance, left, and US First Lady Melania Trump during the 113th annual First Lady's Luncheon in Washington, DC, US, on Thursday, April 23, 2026. The First Lady's Luncheon is an annual bipartisan event hosted by The Congressional Club Museum and Foundation.

Aaron Schwartz/EPA/Bloomberg via Getty Images

The bipartisan event is hosted each year by The Congressional Club Museum and Foundation.

Melania Trump wore an ivory Dior jacket with a black Dolce & Gabbana pencil skirt.

April 25, 2026: Melania Trump appeared alongside Donald Trump at the White House Correspondents' Dinner before a shooting cut the event short.
WASHINGTON, DC - APRIL 25: (L-R) Karoline Leavitt, White House press secretary, Melania Trump and U.S. President Donald Trump attend The White House Correspondents Dinner at Washington Hilton on April 25, 2026 in Washington, DC.

Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for OP

The president, first lady, and other high-ranking administration officials were rushed out of the Washington Hilton ballroom by Secret Service members when shots were heard in the lobby during the dinner.

A suspect was charged with attempted assassination of the president in what is the third known attempt on Donald Trump's life.

Melania Trump later reappeared with Donald Trump in the White House Briefing Room, still wearing her black Dolce & Gabbana tuxedo dress.

April 27, 2026: Donald Trump and Melania Trump welcomed King Charles and Queen Camilla to the White House for a state visit.
WASHINGTON, DC - APRIL 27: (NO UK SALES FOR 28 DAYS) U.S. President Donald Trump and first lady Melania Trump host King Charles III and Queen Camilla for afternoon tea at the White House on day one of their State Visit to the United States of America on April 27, 2026 in Washington, D.C. The visit will include stops at the nation's capital, New York City, and Virginia, arranged to celebrate the United States of America's 250th anniversary of its independence.

Francis Dias/Pool - via Samir Hussein/WireImage/Getty Images

On the first day of the royal visit, the Trumps shared afternoon tea with the king and queen and showed them the new White House beehive. Melania Trump wore a butter-yellow skirt suit by Adam Lippes.

April 28, 2026: The royal visit continued with a state arrival ceremony at the White House, where Melania Trump and Queen Camilla wore similar looks.
WASHINGTON, DC - APRIL 28: Queen Camila, King Charles III, U.S. President Donald Trump and First lady Melania Trump pose on the balcony of the White House during a state arrival ceremony on the South Lawn of the White House on April 28, 2026 in Washington, DC. President Trump and King Charles III will participate in a number of activities including a bilateral meeting in the Oval Office, with the king later addressing a joint meeting of the United States Congress.

Andrew Harnik/Getty Images

The first lady wore a white Ralph Lauren skirt suit with a straw hat, while Queen Camilla wore a mint-green Fiona Clare coatdress with a wide-brimmed hat and a diamond brooch that belonged to Queen Elizabeth.

April 28, 2026: Later that night, the White House hosted a state dinner in the royals' honor.
WASHINGTON, DC - APRIL 28: (L-R) Queen Camilla, King Charles III, U.S. President Donald Trump, and First Lady Melania Trump pose on the Grand Staircase during an official state dinner hosted by the President and First Lady at The White House on day two of the State Visit of King Charles III and Queen Camilla to the United States of America, on April 28, 2026 in Washington, DC. The dinner, part of a trip arranged to celebrate the United States of America's 250th anniversary of its independence, is the first formal white tie event at The White House since President George W. Bush hosted Queen Elizabeth II in 2007.

Samir Hussein/WireImage/Getty Images

Melania Trump's pale-pink Christian Dior gown coordinated with Camilla's fuchsia Fiona Clare dress.

April 30, 2026: Donald Trump and Melania Trump bid farewell to the king and queen at the South Portico of the White House.
Queen Camilla, from left, King Charles III, US President Donald Trump, and First Lady Melania Trump during a departure ceremony at the South Portico of the White House in Washington, DC, US, on Thursday, April 30, 2026. King Charles III on Tuesday called on the US to maintain its leadership role in the world, and to support Ukraine and the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, in a remarkably pointed speech for a monarch that urged Americans to resist the pull of isolationism.

Aaron Schwartz/CNP/Bloomberg via Getty Images

Melania Trump wore a charcoal gray suit from Dior, while Donald Trump's blue tie matched Camilla's pleated Anna Valentine dress.

May 6, 2026: Melania Trump introduced Donald Trump's speech at a Mother's Day event for military mothers.
US President Donald Trump, left, and First Lady Melania Trump arrive for a military Mother's Day event in the East Room of the White House in Washington, DC, US, on Wednesday, May 6, 2026. The US and Iran were circling around a fresh proposal to end the war on Wednesday, as President Donald Trump searches for an exit from a conflict that has spiked energy prices and damaged his political standing.

Yuri Gripas/Abaca/Bloomberg via Getty Images

In her remarks, Melania Trump called mothers "the soul of our nation."

"This is a time of military conflict for America," she said. "And whereby we honor our selfless and valiant Service Members regularly, today is the day we hold their mothers in the highest regard."

May 19, 2026: Melania Trump joined her husband at the annual Congressional Picnic.
US President Donald Trump and US First Lady Melania Trump leave the Congressional Picnic on the South Lawn of the White House in Washington, DC on May 19, 2026.

Kent NISHIMURA/AFP via Getty Images

The first lady wore a pink floral Valentino jumpsuit as she greeted lawmakers on the South Lawn of the White House.

June 9, 2026: Melania Trump hosted the Presidential Artificial Intelligence Challenge National Champion Awards Ceremony.
WASHINGTON, DC - JUNE 9: U.S. first lady Melania Trump presents awards to finalists of the Presidential AI Challenge during an awards ceremony at the White House on June 9, 2026 in Washington, DC. The event, hosted by the first lady, acknowledged the Presidential AI Challenge regional finalists and winners.

Anna Rose Layden/Getty Images

Melania Trump presented awards to six student teams that placed as finalists of the Presidential AI Challenge. The student groups used AI to develop models, including a "Homework Helper" and a "Friendzone Chatbot Bullying Prevention App."

"Today is about opening doors," she said in her speech. "When new doors open, passions flow, courage blossoms, and dreams are realized. AI inspires."

She wore a Dolce & Gabbana pinstripe suit.

June 11, 2026: She appeared at the US Treasury Department to launch Fostering the Future Accounts.
WASHINGTON, DC - JUNE 11: U.S. first lady Melania Trump speaks listens as U.S. Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent speaks during an event at the U.S. Treasury Department on June 11, 2026 in Washington, D.C. The first lady's office held the event to announce the launch of "Fostering the Future Accounts" as part of her Fostering the Future initiative.

Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images

As part of her Fostering the Future initiative, Melania Trump expanded access to Trump accounts — investment accounts for children supported by the US Treasury with a one-time $1,000 deposit — to support foster youth.

She wore a black Dolce & Gabbana blazer, a white skirt by Adam Lippes, and white Christian Louboutin heels.

June 15, 2026: Melania Trump accompanied Donald Trump to UFC Freedom 250.
WASHINGTON, DC - JUNE 15: U.S. President Donald Trump and First Lady Melania Trump leave UFC Freedom 250 on the South Lawn of the White House on June 15, 2026 in Washington, DC. President Trump is hosting a series of Ultimate Fighting Championship matches today, his 80th birthday, which the White House is calling "a once-in-a-generation celebration of the American fighting spirit."

Andrew Harnik/Getty Images

Donald Trump held a series of Ultimate Fighting Championship matches at the White House in honor of his 80th birthday and America's 250th anniversary. The UFC Freedom 250 event was hosted in a temporary 4,000-seat arena built on the South Lawn of the White House.

Melania Trump attended the event wearing a black leather jacket and a black dress, both from Dolce & Gabbana.

July 4, 2026: She attended the "Salute to America" event on the National Mall to celebrate America's 250th birthday.
Donald Trump and Melania Trump at "Salute to America."

Jim Lo Scalzo/EPA/Bloomberg via Getty Images

The president and first lady celebrated America's semiquincentennial at the "Salute to America" event featuring military flyovers, musical performances, and fireworks.

Melania Trump wore a belted, white polka-dot shirtdress by Adam Lippes.

July 19, 2026: Melania Trump kept a lower profile with just one other appearance in July, joining Donald Trump at the FIFA World Cup 2026 Final.
EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - JULY 19: U.S. First Lady Melania Trump, U.S. President Donald Trump, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum pose for photos during the FIFA World Cup 2026 Final match between Spain and Argentina at New York New Jersey Stadium on July 19, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

Eva Marie Uzcategui - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images

Melania Trump and Donald Trump were joined by Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum at the match between Spain and Argentina.

The first lady wore a tan Thom Browne jacket, a white Gap T-shirt, and white Ralph Lauren pants.

While Melania Trump only made two public appearances in July, the Office of the First Lady announced on July 30 that she helped reunite five Ukrainian and Russian children with their families who had been displaced by the ongoing war.

"While diplomacy and peacebuilding are important to this effort, they are surpassed by our collective ability to place children above international disputes," she said in a statement issued by the White House. Every reunion is a reminder that compassion, dignity, and family can transcend even the darkest of times: war."

August 20, 2026: Melania Trump spoke at a Fostering the Future event in the Rose Garden — her first public appearance in 32 days.
US First Lady Melania Trump, left, and US President Donald Trump arrive for a Fostering the Future event in the Rose Garden of the White House in Washington, DC, US, on Thursday, Aug. 20, 2026. The First Lady announced that a $2 million donation from IndyCar and Fox Corporation will fund Fostering the Future scholarships at Indiana University and Purdue University.

Yuri Gripas/Abaca/Bloomberg via Getty Images

At the gathering, Melania Trump announced that IndyCar and Fox Corporation had donated $2 million to fund scholarships at Indiana University and Purdue University through her Fostering the Future initiative.

In her remarks, Melania Trump acknowledged her monthlong absence from the White House.

"Good afternoon. I heard you missed me?" she said. "Here I am."

In a departure from her usual neutral outfits, she wore a blue Michael Kors blouse and a red Dior pencil skirt with matching red Manolo Blahnik heels.

August 23, 2026: She joined Donald Trump at the Freedom 250 Grand Prix Race in Washington, DC.
US President Donald Trump waves the green flag to start the race with First Lady Melania Trump at his side, during the Freedom 250 Grand Prix Race on the streets of Washington, DC, on August 23, 2026. The Freedom 250 Grand Prix is part of celebrations marking the 250th anniversary of US independence. The race will cover 147 laps of a 1.7-mile, seven-turn street circuit around the National Mall, passing landmarks including the US Capitol and Washington Monument. (Photo by Doug MILLS / POOL / AFP via Getty Images)

Doug MILLS/POOL/AFP via Getty Images

Donald Trump waved the green flag to start the race, held on the National Mall, as the first lady stood beside him.

Melania Trump wore a white Louis Vuitton blouse with wide-leg trousers and Roger Vivier Gommettine flats.

September 11, 2026: The president and first lady marked the 25th anniversary of 9/11 at the Pentagon.
US President Donald Trump and First Lady Melania Trump bow their heads during a ceremony to mark the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks at the Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia, US, on Friday, Sept. 11, 2026. President Donald Trump defended the war in Iran during a Pentagon ceremony marking the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11, 2001 attacks, tying the conflict to the US's decades-long fight against terrorism.

Annabelle Gordon/UPI/Bloomberg via Getty Images

While all four living former US presidents attended the 9/11 memorial service at the site of the World Trade Center in New York City, Donald Trump and Melania Trump observed the 25th anniversary of the attacks at the Pentagon. Vice President JD Vance attended the memorial in New York instead. Melania Trump wore a charcoal Dolce & Gabbana pantsuit.

When asked why he was going to the event and not Trump, Vance told reporters that they had "decided as a team" that he would go to New York while Trump stayed in DC to be at the Pentagon.

"Frankly, we'd like to be three or four places on 9/11, but you can't have one person be in multiple locations at the exact same time," Vance said.

September 15, 2026: Melania Trump visited an elementary school in North Carolina.
NORTH JEFFERSON, NORTH CAROLINA - SEPTEMBER 15: U.S. First Lady Melania Trump meets with students at Mountain View Elementary School on September 15, 2026 in North Jefferson, North Carolina. The First Lady is at the school to see how they're using technology in the classroom. (Photo by

Kent Nishmura-Pool/Getty Images

Melania previously visited Mountain View Elementary School after Hurricane Helene in 2024. During this visit, the first lady met with students and spoke about her AI initiatives.

"We may face hard times, but we do not fail," she said. "We choose to grow like a rare young flower pushing through the cold earth after a storm."

She wore a green Nour Hammour leather jacket, a pinstriped Adam Lippes pencil skirt, and Manolo Blahnik pumps.

September 22, 2026: She sat with the US delegation as Donald Trump addressed the 81st United Nations General Assembly.
TOPSHOT - US First Lady Melania Trump (C) sits alongside US Secretary of State Marco Rubio (L) and US Ambasador to the UN Mike Waltz (R) as US President Donald Trump addresses the 81st United Nations General Assembly at the United Nations Headquarters in New York, on September 22, 2026. (Photo by ANGELA WEISS / AFP via Getty Images)

ANGELA WEISS / AFP via Getty Images

At the United Nations Headquarters, the first lady sat between Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz.

She wore a black pantsuit from Dolce & Gabbana with a white blouse from Givenchy.

September 23, 2026: Donald Trump and Melania Trump headed to Joint Base Andrews to welcome Chinese leader Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, for a state visit.
WASHINGTON, DC - SEPTEMBER 23: U.S. President Donald Trump (L) and first lady Melania Trump walk together after returning to the White House on September 23, 2026 in Washington, DC. Trump traveled to Joint Base Andrews, Maryland to welcome Chinese President Xi Jinping as he arrived for a visit to the United States.

Andrew Harnik/Getty Images

Melania Trump paired a Givenchy skirt suit with a white T-shirt from Gap.

September 24, 2026: Melania Trump accompanied Liyuan to the National Museum of Asian Art.
Peng Liyuan, wife of Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Melania Trump, wife of U.S. President Donald Trump, visit the National Museum of Asian Art in Washington, D.C., the United States, Sept. 24, 2026.

Liu Bin/Xinhua via Getty Images

Melania Trump's black skirt suit was designed by Alexander McQueen.

September 24, 2026: That evening, Melania Trump chose a non-traditional outfit for the White House state dinner.
Peng Liyuan, China's first lady, from left, Xi Jinping, China's president, US President Donald Trump, and First Lady Melania Trump during an arrival ceremony at the North Portico of the White House ahead of a state dinner in Washington, DC, US, on Thursday, Sept. 24, 2026. Donald Trump and Xi Jinping agreed to maintain a trade truce until early 2027, with neither ready to upend relations between the world's biggest economies even as tensions persist over rare earths, technology curbs and Taiwan.

Daniel Heuer/Bloomberg via Getty Images

First ladies have historically worn gowns to formal state dinners. Melania Trump broke from tradition with her ensemble featuring black brocade pants and a cummerbund from Hervé Pierre, a white Saint Laurent blouse, and Christian Louboutin stilettos.

Numerous tech leaders attended the state dinner, including Sam Altman, Elon Musk, and Jeff Bezos.

September 25, 2026: The president and first lady visited the National Archives with Jinping and Liyuan.
US-CHINA-DIPLOMACY-TRUMP-XI US President Donald Trump, First Lady Melania Trump, China's President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan stand together as they arrive to visit the National Archives in Washington, DC on September 25, 2026. The rotunda at the National Archives permanently houses the Declaration of Independence, Bill of Rights and the US Constitution.

SAUL LOEB/AFP via Getty Images

The leaders visited the rotunda to view the Declaration of Independence, the Bill of Rights, and the US Constitution.

Melania Trump wore a navy Ralph Lauren pantsuit with Manolo Blahnik heels.

items.title: The AI industry is booming. Women are getting left behind
items.summary: Women hold just a fraction of new AI jobs but are overrepresented in roles with high risk of AI disruption There’s a common fear among people who work in Silicon Valley: snag one of the fast-growing, high-paying jobs in artificial intelligence, or get trapped in the “permanent underclass”, a phrase describing the fate of those who won’t have upward mobility in the age of AI. The phrase usually describes a future in which AI automates human jobs. But for women in tech, it’s starting to look like the present.

items.title: Ex-Trump AI Adviser Sriram Krishnan Targets Raising a $500 Million Venture Fund
items.summary: Sriram Krishnan, a key AI adviser to President Donald Trump who left the White House in June, is raising an AI-focused venture fund, according to three people familiar with the matter. The fund will target raising around $500 million to invest in growth- and later-stage companies, the people said. Before joining the Trump administration, Krishnan worked for tech companies including Microsoft and Twitter. He later became a general partner at Andreessen Horowitz, where he helped launch the venture firm’s London office. At the White House, Krishnan worked under AI and crypto czar David Sacks on the administration’s AI policy, helping to spearhead its AI action plan , released in July 2025.

items.title: Meta Is Refusing to Remove AI-Generated Facebook Videos of Graphic Child Abuse, Including a Baby Roasting in an Oven
items.summary: Content warning: this story contains descriptions of disturbing AI-generated videos that depict violent child abuse. Last month, we reported that Facebook was hosting enormous numbers of graphic AI-generated videos of physical child abuse that showed kids being beaten, burned, dragged by their hair, locked in cages, and more. In response to our questions, Facebook’s parent company Meta alternately dragged its feet, rationalized about why the videos were acceptable, and issued hard-to-parse statements that dodged any accountability or meaningful commitment to fighting the phenomenon. As we reported the story, Meta eventually pulled down an account we shared with it that had uploaded a particularly disturbing array of AI videos that depicted children being viciously beaten and forced to eat trash, as well as many more appalling scenarios including a young girl being locked in a freezer by a kidnapper. But after we published our piece, we were surprised to see that the account had been reinstated, along with its sickening cache of videos. We reached out to Meta to ask why the account was live again and received a curt response from a spokesperson. “Just wanted to let you know that we’re looking into this,” it read. “I’m not sure of an exact timeline, but I will let you know when I learn more.” The account later vanished again, and the spokesperson ignored follow-up questions about why it had been restored to the platform. Untold thousands of similar videos remain on Facebook, and more are being uploaded every day. Curious whether Meta had grown more responsive to reports about the distressing content, yesterday we sent it 19 more accounts loaded with similar child abuse horrors. This time the company didn’t even reply, leaving all the accounts live on Facebook more than 24 hours later when we published this story. It did not respond to a request for comment. The videos, which we are opting not to share, contain a cavalcade of horrors. One shows a baby roasting in an oven, sobbing while its skin blisters from the heat. Another shows a toddler being pushed down the stairs. Another shows a little girl tied to a tree while a woman strikes her with a cast iron pan. Many more clips show children being beaten with belts, ropes, and other household objects, or being locked inside washing machines and dog kennels. “Grandpa, I’m so hungry,” pleads a girl who’s been shut in a pigsty in one of the videos. Another subgenre of video being posted by the accounts we sent Meta depict Black children being beaten and berated by teachers in classroom environments. “Why don’t you go to a school for Black kids?” a teacher demands in one of the videos, after striking a crying Black student with a ruler. “Why do you keep trying to get into a school like this?” (Many of the clips end with an adult stepping in to help the child, which Meta pointed to as justification for the videos in our last story.) If Meta was serious about proactively identifying and removing the videos, it would have immense resources at its disposal to do so. The company has poured hundreds of billions of dollars into developing what its CEO Mark Zuckerberg terms “superintelligence” — AI resources, evidently, that aren’t being marshalled to control the spread of horrifying content on the company’s platforms. In fact, the company could easily flag the child abuse videos simply by looking at the text descriptions that they’re being uploaded with, which often describe the torturous scenes in disarming detail. “My mother put my newborn, who was suffering from a severe fever and chills, into a heated oven to ‘cure the cold,'” reads the caption on the video of the baby in the oven. “Even as the baby screamed and suffered severe burns, she refused to take the child out because she believed her treatment was about to work. When my husband rushed in to rescue our baby, she began smashing things, screaming, and blocking the oven, refusing to let him take the child out.” The videos we identified aren’t the only AI-generated nightmares on Meta’s platforms. Last month, Wired reported that the company had allowed hundreds of advertisements that included overtly sexual material of real children. Add it all up, and Meta — which allows users as young as 13 — feels like a company that’s effectively given up on content moderation. If anything, it just seems annoyed that we keep pointing out its complicity with the horrific content. More on Meta: Meta’s Muse Is Spying on All Your Friends and Family

Content warning: this story contains descriptions of disturbing AI-generated videos that depict violent child abuse.

Last month, we reported that Facebook was hosting enormous numbers of graphic AI-generated videos of physical child abuse that showed kids being beaten, burned, dragged by their hair, locked in cages, and more.

In response to our questions, Facebook’s parent company Meta alternately dragged its feet, rationalized about why the videos were acceptable, and issued hard-to-parse statements that dodged any accountability or meaningful commitment to fighting the phenomenon.

As we reported the story, Meta eventually pulled down an account we shared with it that had uploaded a particularly disturbing array of AI videos that depicted children being viciously beaten and forced to eat trash, as well as many more appalling scenarios including a young girl being locked in a freezer by a kidnapper.

But after we published our piece, we were surprised to see that the account had been reinstated, along with its sickening cache of videos. We reached out to Meta to ask why the account was live again and received a curt response from a spokesperson.

“Just wanted to let you know that we’re looking into this,” it read. “I’m not sure of an exact timeline, but I will let you know when I learn more.”

The account later vanished again, and the spokesperson ignored follow-up questions about why it had been restored to the platform.

Untold thousands of similar videos remain on Facebook, and more are being uploaded every day. Curious whether Meta had grown more responsive to reports about the distressing content, yesterday we sent it 19 more accounts loaded with similar child abuse horrors.

This time the company didn’t even reply, leaving all the accounts live on Facebook more than 24 hours later when we published this story. It did not respond to a request for comment.

The videos, which we are opting not to share, contain a cavalcade of horrors.

One shows a baby roasting in an oven, sobbing while its skin blisters from the heat. Another shows a toddler being pushed down the stairs. Another shows a little girl tied to a tree while a woman strikes her with a cast iron pan. Many more clips show children being beaten with belts, ropes, and other household objects, or being locked inside washing machines and dog kennels.

“Grandpa, I’m so hungry,” pleads a girl who’s been shut in a pigsty in one of the videos.

Another subgenre of video being posted by the accounts we sent Meta depict Black children being beaten and berated by teachers in classroom environments.

“Why don’t you go to a school for Black kids?” a teacher demands in one of the videos, after striking a crying Black student with a ruler. “Why do you keep trying to get into a school like this?”

(Many of the clips end with an adult stepping in to help the child, which Meta pointed to as justification for the videos in our last story.)

If Meta was serious about proactively identifying and removing the videos, it would have immense resources at its disposal to do so. The company has poured hundreds of billions of dollars into developing what its CEO Mark Zuckerberg terms “superintelligence” — AI resources, evidently, that aren’t being marshalled to control the spread of horrifying content on the company’s platforms.

In fact, the company could easily flag the child abuse videos simply by looking at the text descriptions that they’re being uploaded with, which often describe the torturous scenes in disarming detail.

“My mother put my newborn, who was suffering from a severe fever and chills, into a heated oven to ‘cure the cold,'” reads the caption on the video of the baby in the oven. “Even as the baby screamed and suffered severe burns, she refused to take the child out because she believed her treatment was about to work. When my husband rushed in to rescue our baby, she began smashing things, screaming, and blocking the oven, refusing to let him take the child out.”

The videos we identified aren’t the only AI-generated nightmares on Meta’s platforms. Last month, Wired reported that the company had allowed hundreds of advertisements that included overtly sexual material of real children.

Add it all up, and Meta — which allows users as young as 13 — feels like a company that’s effectively given up on content moderation. If anything, it just seems annoyed that we keep pointing out its complicity with the horrific content.

More on Meta: Meta’s Muse Is Spying on All Your Friends and Family

items.title: SoPhi Harness — From Inert Files to Self-Writing Skills: Evolving an AI Agent’s Skill System
items.summary:
Series: Building SoPhi — a Kotlin Agent Harness — Article 07 A general contractor doesn’t wait for a family to pick out a stove before running the gas line to the kitchen. Rough-in work happens before there’s a tenant: the pipe stubs out of the floor where a sink will eventually sit, built to spec and completely inert, because the fixtures that will actually use any of it haven’t been chosen yet. You build for a future occupant you can describe in general terms but haven’t met. sophi-skills Shipped at the very beginning during the skeleton creation as exactly this kind of rough-in work: a place to keep instructions nobody was reading yet. The module did nothing useful the day it landed. It was finished months later by something else entirely — and the gap between "stored" and "read" is where this story actually lives. A recipe box nobody’s cooking from yet A skill in Sophi is a single Markdown file with YAML frontmatter — a recipe card, one file per dish: --- title: "Deploy runbook" description: "How to deploy this service safely" tags: [ops, deploy] --- Steps to deploy... data class Skill( val metadata: SkillMetadata, val body: String, val source: Path ) SkillLoader reads a whole directory of these into memory eagerly — every file, every byte, parsed at startup, sorted by title. SkillRegistry layers a global directory underneath a project directory, project entries winning on ID collision, tolerant of a malformed card runCatching { loader.loadFile(file) }.getOrNull() — one bad recipe doesn't spoil the box). None of that is "lazy" in the way the module's own description implies. What's actually lazy is what happens after loading: a skill's body sits parked in a Map doing nothing until something specifically asks for it. Nobody reads a recipe box front to back before deciding what's for dinner — you pull one card, the one you need, and the rest stay exactly where they were. Zero dependency on the kitchen Here’s the detail that makes the analogy earn its keep instead of just decorating the prose: sophi-skills's pom.xml depends on kotlin-stdlib, a YAML parser, and — since skill versions needed somewhere durable to live — sophi-versioning, itself nothing more than kotlin-stdlib plus a storage abstraction. No sophi-core. No Tool interface. No coroutines, anywhere in that chain. A recipe card doesn't need a stove to exist — it's paper, and Sophi's skill format is the software equivalent, a pure parse-Markdown-into-data-classes module that could sit in a completely different project and still make sense on its own terms. Which meant, for a while, it had no way to get into the kitchen at all. A shelf with no cook yet Skills landed as a loadable data structure with genuinely nothing consuming it — the SkillLoader/SkillRegistry pair shipped, worked, had tests, and had no caller anywhere for weeks. The recipe box existed. Nobody had told the cook it was in the pantry. What eventually gave it a consumer was a plain Tool that lets the model pull a card off the shelf itself — and where that Tool could live turned out to be its own small puzzle: class SkillTool( private val registry: SkillRegistry, private val topK: Int? = null ) : Tool { override val name = "skill" override val description: String = "Load a skill's instructions into context. Available skills:
" + registry.topLevel().let { all -> topK?.let { all.take(it) } ?: all }.joinToString("
") { (id, skill) -> "- $id: ${skill.metadata.description}" } override fun riskLevel(argumentsJson: String) = RiskLevel.SAFE override suspend fun execute(argumentsJson: String): String { val skillName = args?.name ?: return "Error: missing 'name' argument" val skill = registry.get(skillName) ?: return "Error: skill not found: $skillName" val children = registry.childrenOf(skillName) if (children.isEmpty()) return skill.body return skill.body + "

Available in this domain:
" + children.joinToString("
") { (id, child) -> "- $id: ${child.metadata.description}" } } } SkillTool implements sophi-core's Tool and holds a sophi-skills SkillRegistry — sophi-sdk was the only module with an edge to both, so it's the only place that class could compile. SkillTool couldn't live in sophi-skills — the whole point of the previous section was that sophi-skills never learns what a Tool even is. It couldn't stay parked in sophi-cli forever either: ADR-028 (August 25th) gave sophi-companion the same tool set as the terminal, and a class only sophi-cli could see couldn't serve a second host. Registered conditionally — if the pantry's empty, there's no point offering a tool that does nothing: if (skillRegistry.topLevel().isNotEmpty()) { registry.register(SkillTool(skillRegistry, topK = harnessConfig?.topKSkills)) } and a second front door, /skill , that skips asking the model entirely and slides the card straight into the conversation: session.append(EntryRole.TOOL_RESULT, skill.body) output("Injected skill: $sub") Two ways in — the model deciding it wants a recipe mid-turn, or a human handing it one — both reaching the same shelf. Neither existed the week the shelf itself was built, and by the time the first one did, the shelf had grown tabs: SkillRegistry now distinguishes a domain's root card (topLevel()) from its members (childrenOf(domainId)) — ask SkillTool for site-github-com today and it hands back that card plus a list of every sibling card filed under it, the same box now organized as a binder instead of one flat stack of index cards. The box learns to write its own cards Reading a card was the previous milestone’s whole job. Later, the box gained a way to fill itself:write_skill lets the agent record a new site-specific card after it works out how a website behaves — site-github-com, or a domain member like site-maidplus-de/companies — and install_skill pulls a Claude-Code-shaped SKILL.mdin from a local path or git URL and normalizes its frontmatter to match. ADR-030 , on August 27th, is what makes that safe to leave running: static content checks (a secret/credential scan, a prompt-injection-phrase scan for anything arriving from outside the codebase) block a write before a single byte lands, and neither tool got to skip the door article-06 built: override fun riskLevel(argumentsJson: String) = RiskLevel.DESTRUCTIVE on both — a card that changes what a future turn believes about the world doesn’t get to be SAFE just because the box holding it started out inert. install_skill goes one step further and opts out of auto mode's shortcut entirely (ruleVerdict returns HIGH_RISK unconditionally): content arriving from a git URL always gets a human's eyes on it, no exception a classifier gets to grant. Writing a card and judging whether it was any good are two different moments, on two different clocks — no eval suite runs inside write_skill's own execute(). A written card lands as a trial version, not a promoted one — reading it back to check it actually helped is a separate command (sophi skill verify) run on a separate day. That's deliberate, not a missing feature: running an eval suite inside the tool call would stall the turn for minutes waiting on a judgment nobody asked for yet. The verification-and-promotion machinery itself — what the eval suite scores, why it runs twice, how a coverageWarning catches a suite that never actually exercised the new skill — is its own story, not this one. The same bet as its sibling Skills shipping ahead of its own need is exactly the risk rough-in work always takes — you might build for a room that gets used differently than you guessed. It paid off twice over. First, months later, with a Tool and a slash command that needed nothing from sophi-skills itself. Then again a year after that, when the consuming side had to move buildings entirely — sophi-cli to sophi-sdk, then reused unmodified by a second host app that didn't exist when scleton was shipped — and sophi-skills's own code never noticed, because it was never depended on for anything more than Skill and SkillRegistry in the first place. Same instinct as riskLevel's boring SAFE default from article-06 : build the boring, general-purpose thing, leave room, and let whoever moves in next decide what actually goes in the room — even when "whoever" turns out to be a module and a host app that hadn't been designed yet. sophi-extensions — the other half of the previous milestone, a different kind of rough-in entirely, wiring observers into the agent loop instead of storing instructions for it — is its own story, told in the future. What’s next? The next article in this series covers building sub-agents, or as we call it: Calling in a subcontractor: subagents as just another Tool If you’re working on agent-based systems or have thoughts on the build-vs-buy divide in the JVM ecosystem, I’d love to hear your take in the comments below. If this deep dive helped clarify your own architectural choices, a few claps go a long way in helping other engineers find this series. Follow along to stay updated as we build in public. Find the full source on GitHub and connect with me on LinkedIn .
